question: How can organic farming pollute less per field yet cost the planet more per loaf?
answer: Because an organic field grows less. A 2012 analysis in Nature found organic yields about 25% lower on average, from about 5% for some legumes to 34% in the strictest comparisons. The same food then needs more land, and ploughed or cleared land has its own cost. Per field and per tonne can disagree.
move: Judge a method per unit of what it makes, not per field.
ask: Am I measuring my choices per item, when what matters is the total result?
reference: Seufert, Ramankutty & Foley, Comparing the yields of organic and conventional agriculture, Nature, 2012
